verdict.rationale: BigQuery docs say it supports open table formats including Apache Iceberg, Delta and Hudi. Iceberg managed tables keep data in customer-owned storage buckets and allow interoperable access on a single copy, and community users describe querying object-storage data through BigQuery external tables. Missing for 10: any evidence of querying Parquet files directly, detail on how Delta tables are queried in place, and documented external-table mechanics for querying data in object storage without loading it.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I can query open table formats and files in object storage — Iceberg, Delta, Parquet — without first loading them into proprietary storage

citations.quote: supports open table formats like Apache Iceberg, Delta, and Apache Hudi
Iceberg managed tables offer the same fully managed experience as standard BigQuery tables, but store data in customer-owned storage buckets.
Iceberg managed tables support the open Iceberg table format for better interoperability with open-source and third-party compute engines on a single copy of data.
Athena lets you query S3 data like BQ external tables, but BQ is much faster
